messages:
maria: Heads up — starting AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC) control plane + data-plane. Need quick checklist: service account IAM permissions, grant vs policy guidance, envelope rotation plan, and logging/audit surface. Anyone free to advise? cc @samir @anna

samir: I can start. tl;dr: use a dedicated CMK per-customer for control plane metadata, and a separate CMK for dataplane DEK wrapping. Grants for runtime access, key policy for admins.

anna: Agree. Also add: KMS VPC endpoints (kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com) + restrict via kms:ViaService and source VPC condition to tighten.

samir: Minimal IAM for the service principal ("redwood-private-svc"):
```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:GenerateDataKey*","kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:...:key/CMK-ADDR"}
  ]
}
```
Use grants for short-lived worker permissions instead of widening the key policy. Grants avoid IAM policy propagation delays.

maria: For key rotation, do we rewrap existing DEKs automatically or keep old CMK around and rotate DEKs on first use?

anna: Best practice: enable automatic key rotation (annual) on CMK, but implement a rewrap job that iterates active DEKs and re-encrypts with latest CMK if you need immediate rotation. Stagger to avoid IOPS spikes.

samir: Implementation notes:
- Dataplane: each model/container gets ephemeral DEK cached in memory, TTL ~5m, backed by encrypted DEK in storage. Cache TTL depends on latency SLOs.
- Control plane: metadata DEKs can have longer cache TTL, but lock access via RBAC and audit.
- Use KMS grants for workers: CreateGrant with Constraints: {"EncryptionContextSubset": {"tenant":"<tenant-id>"}} to bind usage to tenant.

anna: Audit/logging: enable CloudTrail Data Events for KMS and CloudWatch log group's resource policies to capture decrypt/generateDataKey calls. Ship logs to central S3 bucket (immutable retention) and to SIEM for alerts on unusual patterns.

maria: What about cross-account setups? customers run in their AWS account and we need our control plane to call their KMS.

samir: Cross-account pattern: customers create a CMK in their account, include our service principal ARN in key policy (or use grants via assume-role). Prefer: customer creates role we assume, we call KMS in their account with that role. Avoid putting our principal directly in their key policy unless necessary. Document both options for customers.

anna: Edge case — BYOK (customer-managed key) + external rotation. Clarify that we will not rotate customer CMKs; we only rotate DEKs we generate. If customer rotates CMK, they must provide new CMK ARN or enable rewrap workflow. 

ops-runbook: Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kms-private-integration — includes playbooks for key compromise, rotation, and emergency rewrap. :link:

samir: On grants vs policies: grants are ideal for frequent, ephemeral access. Use grant tokens or CreateGrant with RetiringPrincipal for easier cleanup. Key policy should be restrictive: only admin principals + service admin roles.

maria: Is there a recommended encryption context shape? want to ensure we can audit per-tenant and prevent cross-tenant decrypts.

anna: Yes — require an encryptionContext with tenant_id and component (control_plane|dataplane) and optionally request_id. Enforce via KMS conditions and grant restrictions. Example: {"tenant_id":"t-12345","component":"dataplane"}.

kms-bot: [system] Scheduled CMK rotation for test-customer-01 at 2026-05-10T03:00:00Z. Will trigger rewrap job if enabled.

maria: Last question: DEK cache compromise window and revocation — how to revoke quickly?

samir: Revoke options:
- Revoke grants (if used) — can retire grants to stop new operations but existing cached DEKs remain valid until TTL.
- Shorten DEK cache TTL and issue emergency rewrap for affected tenant.
- For full revocation, rotate CMK and rewrap all DEKs, then expire cached tokens. Document SLOs for revocation (e.g., 30m for soft revoke, 4h for full rewrap).

anna: Also add telemetry: instrument kms:Decrypt error spikes, unusual principals, and failed encryption-context mismatches. Hook to incident channel.

maria: Perfect — I'll draft a short RFC and a checklist from this thread. Thanks @samir @anna. Will link RFC here when ready. :thumbsup:
